roles.heroLead: Shoreline's post-war ramblers hide famously small bathrooms — and small rooms punish shortcuts twice as hard, because every surface is close enough to inspect. Tile and grout will not keep water out of your framing; the bonded membrane behind them does that. We build it, flood it for a documented 24 hours, photograph everything, then set tile that makes 40 square feet feel like 80.

roles.costH2: How much does tile installation cost in Shoreline, WA?
roles.costP1: Count on $14–$26 per square foot installed for Shoreline tile once tile, setting materials, prep and labor are added up; labor by itself starts at $11/sq ft. Tub-shower surrounds generally invoice at $3,200–$6,800, and the full small-bath package — floor, shower, niche — tends to finish between $6,500 and $14,000.
roles.costP2: Counterintuitive but true in small rooms: the tile's shape sets the labor, not its price. A bargain mosaic multiplies cuts and joints until it out-costs a premium plank — and in a 5×8 bath, nearly every tile meets a wall, so cuts dominate.
roles.costNote: Shoreline ranges current for August 2026 — tile, materials and labor together. Small rooms swing on details, so the free written estimate is the number to build plans on.
roles.layersLead: Under the grout of a lasting shower sit seven layers in order. The Shoreline failures we open share one autopsy: a skipped layer — the membrane, usually — traded away for a few hundred dollars and bought back years later at demolition rates.
roles.whyP1: A leak in a compact bath reaches the framing fast — there is simply less distance to travel. Water clears the grout, saturates the substrate, and reports back months later as a spongy hallway strip or a ceiling mark in the room below. The remedy by then is framing, subfloor, drywall and a complete re-tile.
roles.whyP2: The membrane and flood test cost about a tenth of the shower. In a 60-year-old rambler, skipping that tenth is how remodels turn into rebuilds.
roles.scopeIntro: Opening prices — format, what the old floor conceals and layout complexity adjust them. The number worth planning around gets written at your home, free of charge.
roles.cardShower: The full hidden assembly — pre-sloped pan, bonded membrane, overnight flood test with photos — then the tile, niche and curb or curbless entry. Tub-to-shower conversions in small baths are our bread and butter.
roles.cardFloors: Bathrooms, kitchens, entries and basements across the north end. Subfloor flattened first, uncoupling membrane added where post-war framing moves or a heat mat goes in.
roles.cardBacksplash: Subway, stacked, mosaic or slab-look — with tidy outlet cuts, finished edges, and grout keyed to the counter rather than the carton.
roles.cardHeated: Electric mats under tile — resistance-tested before and after setting, dedicated circuit, wall thermostat. In a compact bath the warmth reaches every corner; add it while the floor is open or not at all.
roles.cardRepair: Cracked tiles, tired grout, shower corners letting go. You get a straight verdict: surface repair that will hold, or substrate failure that repair would only paper over.
roles.cardDemo: Down to bare framing: original tile, mortar bed and backer all out, dust pinned behind sheeting and negative air, debris hauled off before dinner. A small bathroom makes a surprising pile — ours never lingers.

roles.faqQ1: How much does tile installation cost in Shoreline, WA?
roles.faqA1: Shoreline tile lands in the $14-to-$26 bracket per square foot installed — one number folding in tile, materials for setting, prep and labor — and at least $11 of every square foot is labor. Tub-shower surrounds tend to fall between $3,200 and $6,800; finish the whole bathroom — floor, shower, niche — and the total usually stops inside $6,500–$14,000. Format outweighs box price here: mosaics and large planks each stack real labor onto what plain 12×12 costs.
roles.faqQ2: How much does it cost to tile a shower in Shoreline?
roles.faqA2: Shoreline's standard alcove showers price out from $3,200 to $6,800 — demolition, bonded waterproofing, pre-sloped pan, setting, niche, grout, all in. Steam, benches, curbless thresholds and floor-to-ceiling stone raise the figure. About a tenth of the total buys waterproofing — and that tenth is what stands off the five-figure repair.
roles.faqQ3: Do you waterproof showers before tiling?
roles.faqA3: Every shower, no exceptions. Spec is a bonded TCNA / ANSI A118.10 system: base with pre-slope, membrane (sheet or liquid) climbing the walls, corners, seams and penetrations closed up — then the drain gets plugged and the pan holds water for 24 photographed hours before tiling. To water, tile and grout are just decoration; the barrier is the membrane.
roles.faqQ4: How long does a bathroom tile job take?
roles.faqA4: Expect four to six working days for a Shoreline bath: demolition with dust protection to start, substrate and waterproofing next with the flood test sitting overnight, one to two days of tile once it clears, then grout, silicone and trim to finish. Hold off using the shower for 24 hours of cure. A floor alone is typically done in one or two days.
roles.faqQ5: Porcelain or ceramic tile — which is better?
roles.faqA5: Underfoot and in the wet, porcelain: below 0.5% water absorption, denser, and far more chip-resistant. On walls and backsplashes, ceramic performs fine for less money. Our Shoreline rule — porcelain for every floor and shower floor, ceramic or glass earning their spot on the vertical.
roles.faqQ6: Can you install a heated tile floor?
roles.faqA6: Yes — an electric radiant mat over uncoupling membrane comes to roughly $11 to $16 per square foot with thermostat and installation. Resistance gets tested twice — pre-set and post-set — and the mat runs on its own circuit. Small Shoreline bathrooms feel the effect most, and the affordable window for adding it closes the moment the floor is closed.
roles.faqQ7: Do I need to remove the old tile first?
roles.faqA7: In most cases, yes. At around $3.50 per square foot with haul-away included, demolition is what lets us see the subfloor — rot, movement, level — and keep finished heights correct at doorways, which matters doubly in small rooms. Overlaying old tile is possible on a flat, sound, well-bonded base, but it raises the floor and buries what we would rather find early.
roles.faqQ8: How much does a kitchen backsplash cost in Shoreline?
roles.faqA8: Standard backsplashes near 30 square feet cost Shoreline kitchens $1,100 to $2,200 — with outlet cutouts, trimmed edges and color-matched grout in the price. Bids climb when the layout does: think herringbone, sheet mosaic, a mitered frame detail at the cooktop, or ceiling-run slab-look porcelain — the hours sit in cutting and pattern work.
roles.faqQ9: Can you fix cracked tile or regrout instead of replacing?
roles.faqA9: Often — starting near $8 per square foot. Good candidates: discolored or crumbling grout, a tile or two cracked by impact, shower corners ready for grout-out-silicone-in. Bad candidates: hollow-sounding floors, tiles releasing in a spreading pattern, walls that give when pressed — those mean the substrate is done, repairs only buy months, and we will name which case is yours before quoting.
roles.faqQ10: Which Shoreline neighborhoods do you tile?
roles.faqA10: All of Shoreline — Richmond Beach, Innis Arden, Richmond Highlands, Hillwood, Highland Terrace, Echo Lake, Meridian Park, Westminster Triangle, Parkwood, Ridgecrest, North City, Briarcrest, Ballinger and The Highlands — plus Lake Forest Park, Broadview and, beyond them, Seattle, Edmonds, Kenmore and the north end at large.
roles.faqQ11: What warranty comes with tile installation?
roles.faqA11: Every tile installation is backed by our 2-year workmanship warranty — set longer than our carpet term deliberately, because tile issues surface in year two, not week two. When we install a manufacturer's full waterproofing assembly, its system warranty applies as well, and our stored photos of the membrane and flood test preserve the evidence for as long as you own the house.
